questions.question: A runner has the same rank, 26, from both ends of a finishing list. How many runners finished?
questions.explanation: There are 25 runners on each side and the runner herself: 25 + 1 + 25 = 51.

questions.question: A and B occupy the 13th place from the left and 16th from the right in a 54-person row. How many people lie outside the segment from A to B, excluding neither endpoint from that segment?
questions.explanation: Outside people are 12 before A and 15 after B: 12 + 15 = 27.

questions.question: In a row of 41, A is left 6, B left 17 and C left 30. First A swaps with B, then A with C. Which person is now exactly midway between the other two named persons?
questions.explanation: The final places are B = 6, C = 17 and A = 30. The midpoint of 6 and 30 is 18, so no named person is exactly midway.

questions.question: 6 people have distinct heights. Exactly 2 are taller than J. K is shorter than J but taller than L and M; N is taller than J. What is K’s rank from the shortest end?
questions.explanation: J is third tallest; K, L and M are the three below J, with K tallest among them. Thus K is third shortest.

questions.question: A journey starts at 11:50 am and ends at 2:25 pm the same day. How many minutes of the journey occur after 12 noon?
questions.explanation: From noon to 2:25 pm is 2 hours 25 minutes = 145 minutes. The 10 minutes before noon are excluded.

questions.question: P and Q are left 12 and 28. P moves 5 places right while Q moves 4 places left, without crossing each other. How many people are between them now?
questions.explanation: New positions are 17 and 24. Between = 24 - 17 - 1 = 6.

questions.question: A row has 64 applicants. J is 27th from the front. Applicants at original ranks 1 through 8 and 49 through 64 leave. Then the remaining row is reversed. What is J’s new rank from the front?
questions.explanation: Remaining original ranks are 9 through 48, totalling 40. J is 27 - 8 = 19th before reversal, then 40 - 19 + 1 = 22nd.

questions.question: At a school assembly, girl A is 11th from the left and girl B is 29th from the left. A and B are respectively 4th and 12th among girls from that end. How many boys stand strictly between them?
questions.explanation: There are 29 - 11 - 1 = 17 people between them, including 12 - 4 - 1 = 7 girls. Boys = 17 - 7 = 10.

questions.question: A Moga recruitment form is submitted on 8 June. Verification occurs on the third day after submission, and approval 2 days after verification. On which date is approval given?
questions.explanation: Verification is 8 + 3 = 11 June; approval is 11 + 2 = 13 June.

questions.question: A clinic appointment is shifted 25 minutes later. M arrives 8 minutes before the revised time, at 11:47. What was the original appointment time?
questions.explanation: Revised time = 11:47 + 8 = 11:55. Original time = 11:55 - 25 = 11:30.

questions.question: Two aligned rows of 15 face each other. Row I faces north and Row II south. P is 4th from his own left in Row I; Q is opposite P. A new queue takes all of Row I first, then all of Row II, each row in the order of its members’ own left to right. What is Q’s new front rank?
questions.explanation: Opposite facing makes Q 15 - 4 + 1 = 12th from his own left. The first row contributes 15 people, so Q’s new rank is 15 + 12 = 27.

questions.question: A clerk records positions for a 50-person row. Which pair (left rank, right rank) is inconsistent?
questions.explanation: Valid opposite-end ranks add to 51. Only 26 + 24 = 50 fails this rule.

questions.question: An office clock always shows 09:18 at actual 09:30. How many minutes must be added to any reading to obtain actual time?
questions.explanation: The clock is 09:30 - 09:18 = 12 minutes slow, so add 12 minutes.

questions.question: Consider 70 applicants: A is 18th from the left and B is 20th from the right. If all people strictly between A and B leave, how many remain?
questions.explanation: B is left 51, so 51 - 18 - 1 = 32 leave. Remaining = 70 - 32 = 38.

questions.question: At actual 09:20 a clock is 12 minutes fast. It then loses 8 minutes every 4 true hours at a constant rate. When it shows 16:47 later that day, what is its error?
questions.explanation: The display advances from 09:32 to 16:47, or 435 minutes. True elapsed = 435 × 60/58 = 450 minutes; the clock loses 15 minutes, changing its error from +12 to -3 minutes.

questions.question: Parcels A, B, C and D weigh 10, 20, 30 and 40 kg in some order. A is heavier than B; C is heavier than D; B is lighter than D; A and C together weigh 60 kg. Which parcel is heaviest?
questions.explanation: A and C must weigh 20 and 40 kg. B < D fixes B = 10 and D = 30, so C > D forces C = 40 kg.

questions.question: A moves forward in a queue from 24th to 18th. How many other people change their ranks because of this single move?
questions.explanation: The 6 people originally at ranks 18 through 23 each move back one place.

questions.question: A machine completes 3 runs of 42 minutes each. Between consecutive runs it cools for 9 minutes. If the first run starts at 20:18, when does the third finish?
questions.explanation: 3 runs and 2 cooling gaps take 3 × 42 + 2 × 9 = 144 minutes. 20:18 + 2:24 = 22:42.

questions.question: A, B, C and D occupy left positions 4, 14, 23 and 34. A swaps with B, B with C, and C with D. Which pair ends with exactly 8 people between them?
questions.explanation: Final places are A = 14, B = 23, C = 34 and D = 4. Only A-B have positional gap 9, hence 8 between.

questions.question: A departure clock is 9 minutes fast and shows 21:54. An arrival clock is 7 minutes slow and shows 23:08 on the same date. What is the true journey duration in minutes?
questions.explanation: Actual departure is 21:45 and actual arrival is 23:15. Their difference is 90 minutes.

questions.question: Ranks follow competition ranking: tied candidates share a rank, and the next rank skips the occupied places. 6 candidates scored above Leena and 2 others tied with her. What rank does Leena receive?
questions.explanation: A competition rank is one more than the number strictly above: 6 + 1 = 7. Tied candidates share rank 7.

questions.question: A row of 36 is split into two groups: original odd positions form one row and original even positions another, preserving order. P was originally 26th. What is P’s rank from the back in the even-position row?
questions.explanation: The even row has 18 people; P is 26/2 = 13th from its front. Back rank = 18 - 13 + 1 = 6.

questions.question: A is 11th from the left and B is 9th from the right. The row has more than 20 but fewer than 27 people. A lies left of B, with an odd number between them. How many totals satisfy all conditions?
questions.explanation: The gap is N - 11 - 9 = N - 20. For N = 21 through 26 it is odd only at N = 21, 23 and 25.

questions.question: Two friends agree to meet at 17:00. S comes 12 minutes early and waits 20 minutes before leaving. T comes 11 minutes late. How long after S leaves does T arrive?
questions.explanation: S arrives at 16:48 and leaves at 17:08. T arrives at 17:11, which is 3 minutes later.

questions.question: Two rows each have 12 seats numbered from the same fixed left. X is 5th from the right in Row II. Row II is reversed end-to-end first. They then merge in pairs as I1, I2, II1, II2, I3, I4, II3, II4, and continue in that pattern. What is X’s final front rank?
questions.explanation: X starts at II8 and becomes II5 after reversal. 2 complete four-person blocks take 8 places; I5, I6 and II5 take the next 3, so X is 11th.
